chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Aban, from Lays al-Muradi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah had granted Abu Sa'id al-Khudri this insight (or judgment), and his soul's extraction (death pangs) had become severe for him. So he said, 'Carry me to my prayer-mat.' So they carried him, and he did not long remain before he died.

key_terms.الرَّأْي: Insight, judgment, or piety, or sound judgment
key_terms.مُصَلَّاهُ: His prayer-mat or place of prayer
key_terms.نَزْع: Extraction (of the soul), referring to the process of dying

ai.seo_question: What happened to Abu Sa'id al-Khudri during his final moments according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the virtue of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, noting that Allah granted him 'ra'y' (insight or good judgment), which Shia scholars often interpret as spiritual clarity or specific knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt. The account emphasizes the physical difficulty of death (sakarat al-mawt) and the Sunnah of facilitating a dignified passing by positioning the dying person towards their place of prayer, reflecting the practical application of mercy in end-of-life care.
